page: Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd is a bare metal server configured with a dedicated AMD EPYC 9254 processor featuring 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 2.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage consists of a 960 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture is x86_64 and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 extensions) and secure virtualization via AMD SVM, though it lacks Intel-specific AMX features.

In benchmark evaluations, this bare metal configuration demonstrates strong processing and memory capabilities. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance registers in the top 10% tier at 3473.59, while multi-core performance reaches 83358.94, placing it in the top 25%. Memory subsystem performance is notable, with a PassMark memory score of 3310.61 (top 10%) and uncached large-block read bandwidth of 296.64 GB/sec. For database workloads, the system handles 72.25 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a PassMark database operations score of 24811.77. Large-model LLM inference is constrained by the lack of a dedicated GPU, but CPU-based inference on smaller 135M models achieves top-tier speeds of 4386.48 tokens per second for prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the bare metal architecture provides dedicated hardware access without virtualization overhead, maximizing the return on the 384.0 GB DDR5 memory and 48 vCPUs. However, the 960 GB local SSD capacity is relatively modest given the high compute and memory specifications, representing a potential storage bottleneck for data-heavy deployments. This server is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and CPU-bound machine learning inference on small-to-medium models.
